ai.description: This 3–4 cm frog has a triangular body with a dark brown back featuring yellow or orange marbled patterns. It is distinguished by a narrow, pointed snout and a smooth, glandular belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uperodon triangularis* is best distinguished by the prominent, bright yellow or orange triangular patch on its back, which contrasts sharply with its dark brown body.
ai.habitat: The Malabar Ramanella inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Malabar Ramanella is primarily nocturnal and often retreats into tree hollows or rock crevices during the day to avoid desiccation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uperodon triangularis* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs in tree holes or water-filled depressions using an aquatic larval mode.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uperodon triangularis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring in states like Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka at elevations between 100 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Malabar Ramanella emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "peep-peep" notes, typically heard from water-filled tree holes or ground depressions in moist forests.
